claims.text: Weighted to represent the U.S. population, 52.9% of respondents chose the human doctor specialist clinic and 47.1% chose the AI clinic.
Explaining that the AI system has proven superior accuracy compared to human specialists increases the odds of AI provider selection (OR = 1.48, CI: 1.24-1.77, p < .001).
A primary care physician nudging the patient towards AI as the established and recommended choice increases the odds of AI provider selection (OR = 1.25, CI: 1.05-1.50, p = .013).

Reassuring patients that the AI clinic includes trained staff who carefully listen to their lifestyle, preferences, values, and goals increases the odds of AI selection (OR = 1.27, CI: 1.07-1.52, p = .008).
Disease severity does not have a statistically significant effect on AI provider uptake.
A PCP promising to incorporate and explain the AI advice rather than deferring to a patient portal does not have a statistically significant effect on AI provider uptake.
Describing the AI system as racially unbiased does not have a statistically significant main effect on AI provider uptake.
Describing the AI system as financially unbiased does not have a statistically significant main effect on AI provider uptake.
Describing the AI system as using 36 tailored measurements does not have a statistically significant main effect on AI provider uptake.
Compared to White respondents, Black respondents have significantly lower odds of selecting AI (OR = 0.73, CI: 0.55-0.96, p = .023).
Compared to White respondents, Native American respondents have significantly higher odds of selecting AI (OR = 1.37, CI: 1.01-1.87, p = .041).
Older respondents have significantly lower odds of choosing AI (OR = 0.99, CI: 0.987-0.999, p = .03).
Politically conservative respondents have significantly lower odds of choosing AI (OR = 0.65, CI: 0.52-0.81, p < .001).
Respondents who view religion as important have significantly lower odds of choosing AI (OR = 0.64, CI: 0.52-0.77, p < .001).
Higher education level is associated with significantly higher odds of selecting an AI provider (OR = 1.10, CI: 1.03-1.18, p = .004).
Higher trust in AI companies is associated with significantly increased odds of choosing an AI provider (OR = 1.29, CI: 1.23-1.36, p < .001).

methodologies.name: Qualitative Semi-Structured Patient Interviews
methodologies.description: Conducted 30-60 minute structured interviews with 24 racially and ethnically diverse clinic patients to pre-test vignettes and generate hypotheses.

methodologies.name: Factorial Vignette Survey Experiment
methodologies.description: Administered a pre-registered, blinded, randomized survey experiment manipulating eight clinical vignette variables with two levels each on a matched sample of 2,675 U.S. adults oversampling minoritized groups.
datasets: YouGov survey sample (N = 2,675 matched; N = 2,472 analyzed after engagement screening)
conditions: AI accuracy (Proven more accurate vs. Silent)
AI listens (45-min counselor interview vs. Silent)
AI racial unbiased (Tested unbiased vs. Silent)
AI financial unbiased (Tested unbiased vs. Silent)

limitations.text: The qualitative interview pre-study relied on a small convenience sample of 24 patients in one city, preventing strong independent conclusions.
Respondents may find it difficult to accurately predict their real-world medical decisions from hypothetical vignettes, especially in high-emotion contexts.

The Native American sample was older and more conservative than the national average for that group and had the smallest sample size among the racial groups, introducing potential unmeasured confounding.
Neither scenario represented an acute or emergent clinical condition, where patient deference to physicians might differ.

Excluding respondents familiar with the tested conditions as originally pre-registered was not feasible because an unexpectedly large portion (N = 998) was familiar, which would have compromised statistical power and balance.
Prior research shows patients typically prefer human doctors over AI-powered machines and report less willingness to schedule appointments with automated decision aids.

future_work.text: Conduct studies with larger Native American samples to better understand the higher AI uptake observed in that population.
Investigate acute or emergent clinical situations to assess whether patient deference and AI uptake differ.
Research the best methods for physician incorporation of AI and drivers of physician uptake to inform clinical practice and shared decision-making.
